q: What are the direction cosines of the vector 2i − 3j + 6k?
x: |v| = √(4 + 9 + 36) = 7, so the direction cosines are 2/7, −3/7, 6/7. Check: their squares add to 49/49 = 1. Dividing by 2 + 3 + 6 = 11 instead of the magnitude gives the last triple.

q: A vector OP has length 6, makes angles of 60° with the x-axis and 45° with the y-axis, and makes an acute angle with the z-axis. What is OP?
x: cos²γ = 1 − ¼ − ½ = ¼ and γ is acute, so cos γ = ½. OP = 6(½ i + (√2/2) j + ½ k) = 3i + 3√2j + 3k. A negative k-component would make the angle with the z-axis obtuse.

q: What is the distance between the points A(1, −2, 3) and B(3, 1, −3)?
x: AB = 2i + 3j − 6k, so |AB| = √(4 + 9 + 36) = √49 = 7. Leaving out the z-part gives √13.

q: Which of these triples can be the direction cosines of a line?
x: Direction cosines must satisfy l² + m² + n² = 1. Only 1/3 + 1/3 + 1/3 = 1 works; ½, ½, ½ gives 3/4 and 1/3, 2/3, 1/3 gives 6/9.

q: A = (1, 2, 3) and B = (4, −1, 6). What is the point that divides AB internally in the ratio 2 : 1?
x: P = (1·A + 2·B)/3 = ((1 + 8)/3, (2 − 2)/3, (3 + 12)/3) = (3, 0, 5). Swapping the weights gives (2, 1, 4), the 1 : 2 point; (7, −4, 9) is the external point.

q: What is the unit vector in the direction of a + b, where a = 2i + 2j − 5k and b = 2i + j + 3k?
x: a + b = 4i + 3j − 2k, whose magnitude is √(16 + 9 + 4) = √29, so the unit vector is (4i + 3j − 2k)/√29. Dividing by 5 ignores the k-part.

q: a and b are non-zero vectors that are not parallel, and (x − 2)a + (y + 1)b = 3a − 2b. What are x and y?
x: Because a and b are not parallel, the coefficients can be compared: x − 2 = 3 and y + 1 = −2, so x = 5 and y = −3.

q: What is the value of i · i + j · k?
x: i · i = |i|² = 1, and j · k = 0 because j and k are perpendicular. The total is 1.

q: What is the angle between a diagonal of a cube and an edge of the cube drawn from the same corner?
x: Take the unit cube at the origin: diagonal i + j + k, edge i. cos θ = 1/(√3 × 1) = 1/√3. cos⁻¹(√2/√3) is the angle between the diagonal and a face diagonal, and cos⁻¹(1/3) the angle between two diagonals.

q: Which statement is true about the triangle with vertices A(2, 3, 1), B(1, 1, 1) and C(3, 0, 4)?
o: It has a right angle at B
It has a right angle at A
It has a right angle at C
x: BA = i + 2j and BC = 2i − j + 3k, so BA · BC = 2 − 2 + 0 = 0: a right angle at B. AB · AC = 5 and CA · CB = 14 are not zero.

q: For non-zero vectors a and b, when is |a + b|² = |a|² + |b|²?
o: When a and b are parallel
When a and b are perpendicular
x: |a + b|² = |a|² + 2a · b + |b|², so the equality holds exactly when a · b = 0, i.e. a ⊥ b. This is the vector form of Pythagoras' theorem.

q: Forces F₁ = i + 2j + 3k and F₂ = 2i − j + k act together on a particle, which moves from A(0, 1, 2) to B(2, 3, 1). What is the total work done?
x: Resultant F = 3i + j + 4k and displacement AB = 2i + 2j − k, so W = 6 + 2 − 4 = 4 units. Using F₁ alone gives 3.

q: A force of 10 N acts in the direction of 3i + 4j and moves a particle from the origin to the point (2, 1), distances in metres. What is the work done?
x: F = 10(3i + 4j)/5 = 6i + 8j, so W = F · d = 6 × 2 + 8 × 1 = 20 J. Using 3i + 4j itself as the force gives 10 J.

q: What is i × (i × j)?
x: i × j = k, and then i × k = −j. Taking i × k = j (wrong cyclic order) gives j.

q: What is the sine of the angle between a = i + j and b = j + k?
x: a × b = i − j + k, of magnitude √3, and |a||b| = √2 × √2 = 2, so sin θ = √3/2. Check: cos θ = a · b/2 = ½, so θ = 60°.

q: The parallelogram with adjacent sides i + j and λi + 2j has area 3. What are the possible values of λ?
x: (i + j) × (λi + 2j) = (2 − λ)k, so |2 − λ| = 3, giving λ = −1 or λ = 5. Keeping only one sign of the absolute value loses a solution.

q: A = (1, 1, 1), B = (2, 3, 4) and C = (3, 5, 7). What is the area of triangle ABC?
x: AB = i + 2j + 3k and AC = 2i + 4j + 6k = 2AB, so AB × AC = 0 and the area ½|AB × AC| is 0: the points are collinear. √14 is the length of AB, not an area.

q: For vectors with a ≠ 0, it is given that a × b = a × c. What must be true?
o: b − c = ka for some scalar k
x: a × (b − c) = 0, so b − c is parallel to a (or zero): b − c = ka. b need not equal c, for example i × j = i × (i + j).

q: For vectors a, b and c, what does a · (b × c) = 0 tell us?
o: The vectors all have the same length
The vectors are all unit vectors
x: |a · (b × c)| is the volume of the parallelepiped on a, b and c. Zero volume means the three vectors lie in one plane. Mutually perpendicular non-zero vectors give a non-zero volume.

q: If [a b c] = a · (b × c) = 5, what is b · (a × c)?
x: b · (a × c) = [b a c], and swapping two vectors changes the sign: [b a c] = −[a b c] = −5. Only cyclic changes such as [b c a] keep the value 5.

q: The parallelepiped with edges a, b and c from one corner has volume 12. What is the volume of the tetrahedron that has the same three edges from one vertex?
x: Tetrahedron volume = (1/6)|[a b c]| = 12/6 = 2. Using 1/3 gives 4 and using 1/2 gives 6.

q: Let a = i + j + k and b = i − j + k. Which vector is coplanar with a and b?
x: 3i − j + 3k = a + 2b, so it lies in the plane of a and b. Check with triple products: [a, b, i] = 2, [a, b, j + k] = −2 and [a, b, k] = −2, none of them zero.

q: What is the volume of the tetrahedron with vertices A(1, 1, 1), B(2, 1, 1), C(1, 2, 1) and D(1, 1, 3)?
x: Edges from A: AB = i, AC = j, AD = 2k, with triple product 2. Volume = 2/6 = 1/3. Forgetting the 1/6 gives 2.

q: A particle has position r(t) = 2t i + t² j + 3k. What is its acceleration?
x: r′(t) = 2i + 2tj and r″(t) = 2j, a constant. 2i + 2tj is the velocity, not the acceleration.

q: A particle has position r(t) = t i + t² j. At what time are its velocity and acceleration perpendicular?
x: v = i + 2tj and a = 2j, so v · a = 4t, which is zero only at t = 0. There the velocity i is along the x-axis and the acceleration 2j along the y-axis.

q: For r(t) = cos t i + sin t j + t k, what is d/dt(|r(t)|²)?
x: |r|² = cos²t + sin²t + t² = 1 + t², whose derivative is 2t. Check: 2r · r′ = 2(−cos t sin t + sin t cos t + t) = 2t.

q: A particle moves with position r(t) = eᵗ cos t i + eᵗ sin t j. What is its speed at time t?
x: v = eᵗ(cos t − sin t)i + eᵗ(sin t + cos t)j, and |v|² = e^(2t)[(cos t − sin t)² + (sin t + cos t)²] = 2e^(2t). So the speed is √2 eᵗ. Forgetting the product rule gives eᵗ.

q: A projectile has position r(t) = 3t i + (4t − 5t²) j. What is its speed at the instant its velocity is horizontal?
x: v = 3i + (4 − 10t)j is horizontal when t = 0.4, and then v = 3i, so the speed is 3. 5 is the starting speed √(9 + 16).
